name: Do I need to prime bathroom walls before painting?

mainEntity.name: Do I need to prime bathroom walls before painting?

acceptedAnswer.text: A primer is necessary if you are painting over bare drywall, covering water stains, patching holes, or transitioning from oil-based to latex paint. In high-humidity environments, a moisture-blocking, stain-inhibiting primer seals the surface and prevents previous moisture rings from bleeding through your topcoat. If your bathroom walls are already painted with intact latex paint in a similar color, a self-priming bathroom paint may suffice. However, priming is always recommended around showers, vents, and baseboards where peeling or steam damage commonly begins.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, you need primer over bare drywall, patched areas, water stains, or when switching paint types to ensure moisture resistance and strong adhesion.
